title: Electric Charges and Fields: Chapter Introduction
subject: Physics
objective: A rubbed comb lifts paper bits without touching them. Rubbing moves electrons, a charged body attracts even neutral paper by induction, and every charge reaches out through its electric field.

fill.q: Rubbing a plastic comb with dry hair transfers ____ to the comb.
A charged body attracting a neutral body is explained by ____.
In Coulomb's law, the force varies inversely as the ____ of the distance.
Electric field lines start on ____ charges and end on negative charges.

tf.q: A neutral piece of paper cannot be attracted by a charged comb.
tf.explain: Induction makes the nearer side oppositely charged, so it is attracted.
One of the basic properties of charge.

tf.q: Two electric field lines can cross each other.
tf.explain: At a crossing the field would have two directions, which is impossible.

tf.q: Doubling the distance between two charges halves the force.
tf.explain: F ∝ 1/r², so the force becomes one-fourth.

ar.a: A charged comb attracts small bits of paper.
ar.r: Charges in the paper shift, so the nearer side is oppositely charged.
ar.explain: R is the induction that explains A.

ar.a: Field lines from a positive charge point outward.
ar.r: Field lines start on positive charges.
ar.explain: R explains the direction in A.

mcq.q: A comb rubbed with dry hair becomes negative because it:
mcq.explain: Only electrons move when bodies are rubbed.

mcq.q: If both charges are doubled and the distance is unchanged, the force becomes:
mcq.explain: F ∝ q₁q₂, so it becomes 2 × 2 = 4 times.

The force on a charge q₀ in an electric field E is:

num.q: Two charges exert a force of 36 N on each other. Find the force when the distance between them is tripled.
Find the force between two charges of 1 μC each placed 0.3 m apart in air (k = 9 × 10⁹ N m² C⁻²).
A charge of 2 μC is placed in a field of 5 × 10³ N/C. Find the force on it.

short.q: Explain why a rubbed comb lifts bits of paper.
short.solution: Rubbing transfers electrons from the hair to the comb, so the comb is negative. Near it, charges in the neutral paper shift: positive charge nearer, negative farther. The nearer attraction is stronger than the farther repulsion, so the paper is pulled up (induction).

short.q: What is an electric field? How does it explain force without contact?
short.solution: The region around a charge where another charge experiences a force; E = F/q₀. The charge does not need to touch: its field exists in the space around it and acts on any charge placed there.
